correctness.rationale: For any point the section is a two-endpoint chain, a 3-element chain, a 4-element Boolean diamond, or a coatom fan of size at least 3; in the last case an individual coatom lacks a greatest disjoint companion. For admissible sections the minimal-upper-bound characterization gives nonsingleton implication exactly on ordered distinct twin points with a common two-block neighborhood, and the complements swap those blocks. Graph specialization reduces twins to double-edge components. The connected-component labelled EGF follows from exact isolated/path/cycle/double-edge counts. For the Poisson limit, coefficient monotonicity and a positive-weight expansion prove fixed-shift coefficient ratio convergence; the exact factorial moments \(2^{-r}b_{n-2r}/b_n\) then converge, uniformly dominated, to Poisson moments. The standalone verifier replayed successfully from its actual package path and checked 441 incidence systems, 419 admissible graph operations, and exact EGF coefficients. Limits: only the specified incidence family and graph probability model are covered; finite tests are not infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural failure of single-valuedness in the established I-algebra implication is converted from anecdotal small examples into a complete structural classification and exact natural invariant on all finite point–block incidence posets. The allowable degree bound is forced by interval pseudocomplements, not a selected slice. The graph realization gives a precise finite counting law and a nondegenerate limiting probability of globally sharp implication, making a meaningful model-theoretic/logic distinction. The result is self-contained and unrestricted in incidence and graph sizes, while its stated scientific scope is modest.
